requirements.requirement: The system must retrieve distance (in miles) and duration (in minutes) for each clinical trial using the existing Google Routes integration in clinical_trials_service.
The system must compute a raw proximity score for each trial using both distance and duration as inputs.
The system must apply an inverse relationship where shorter distance and duration produce higher raw proximity scores.
The system must combine distance and duration using a deterministic weighting function (e.g., weighted sum or similar) that produces consistent outputs for identical inputs.
The system must normalize proximity scores across all trials in a result set to a 0–100 scale.
The system must ensure that the highest-ranked (closest) trial in a result set receives a normalized score of 100.
The system must ensure that normalized scores preserve relative ordering of trials based on raw proximity scores.
The system must handle a single-trial result set by assigning a normalized score of 100.
The system must treat zero distance or zero duration values as valid inputs and compute a maximum or near-maximum proximity score without error.
The system must handle missing distance or duration data from Google Routes by excluding the trial from scoring or assigning a null proximity score.
The system must not crash when Google Routes returns an error and must return proximity scores for remaining valid trials.
The system must ensure that all computed normalized scores are bounded between 0 and 100 inclusive.
The system must produce identical proximity scores for identical input datasets across repeated executions.
The system must compute proximity scores for all trials in a result set within a single service call without requiring additional external requests beyond Google Routes.
